review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–135) and the downstream users in RestrictedLevelCompactFunctoriality.lean and CompactExceptionalTateCoefficientMaps.lean. I checked how id/comp of invariants maps and of `.hom` are used there. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether `simp` can already close these goals through the `Rep` and `Functor.map_id` simp sets. The proposals add lemmas and leave existing orientations alone. `mapInvariants_coe` and `forget` with `@[simps]` look fine. `toRepHom` is an abbrev for `f.hom`, so it should not create competing simp normal forms.

findings.declaration: instance : Category (LevelCompactRep R G) (inline `hmap` proofs for id and comp)
findings.excerpt:
have hmap : invariantsMap (f.hom ≫ g.hom) U =
            (invariantsMap g.hom U).comp (invariantsMap f.hom U) := by
findings.problem: The functoriality of the invariants map (`invariantsMap (𝟙 _) U = LinearMap.id`, `invariantsMap (f ≫ g) U = (invariantsMap g U).comp (invariantsMap f U)`) is proved only as anonymous `have`s inside the Category instance. No named, `@[simp]` lemmas `mapInvariants_id` / `mapInvariants_comp` exist, so `simp` cannot normalise `mapInvariants (𝟙 A) U` or `mapInvariants (f ≫ g) U`. Downstream, RestrictedLevelCompactFunctoriality.lean re-proves the same two facts as `private` lemmas by an identical `change … rw [Functor.map_id] … rfl` script. Its `coefficientMap_id` and `coefficientMap_comp` then need manual `change`/`rw`/`rfl` instead of `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Before the Category instance, add `@[simp] lemma invariantsMap_id` and `@[simp] lemma invariantsMap_comp` for `invariantsMap`. The first says `invariantsMap (𝟙 A) U = LinearMap.id`. The second says `invariantsMap (f ≫ g) U = (invariantsMap g U).comp (invariantsMap f U)`. Their proofs are the existing `change … rw [Functor.map_id/map_comp] … rfl` scripts. Optionally add `mapInvariants_id` and `mapInvariants_comp` for categorical `𝟙 A` and `f ≫ g`. Use these lemmas in the instance with `rw [invariantsMap_id]` / `rw [invariantsMap_comp]`, and delete the private copies downstream. The orientation (composite to composition of linear maps) is terminating and is the canonical form.
findings.benefit: The two identities live in one public place and `simp` can use them. The duplicated private lemmas downstream go away. Goals such as `coefficientMap_id` and `coefficientMap_comp` can be closed by a short `simp`-based proof instead of a `change`/`rw`/`rfl` script.

findings.declaration: instance : Category (LevelCompactRep R G) / structure Hom (missing `id_hom` and `comp_hom` simp lemmas)
findings.problem: The category structure is defined with `hom := 𝟙 A.rep` and `hom := f.hom ≫ g.hom`. There are no `@[simp]` lemmas `(𝟙 A : A ⟶ A).hom = 𝟙 A.rep` and `(f ≫ g).hom = f.hom ≫ g.hom`, which are the standard simp interface for a bundled Hom structure (the usual `id_hom` / `comp_hom`). The `@[simp] mapInvariants_coe` lemma rewrites to `f.hom x`. For a composite, `(f ≫ g).hom x` is stuck, because the projection of the `Category.comp` instance is not exposed to `simp`. `forget_map` has the same problem. The downstream proofs `coefficientMap_comp` and `coefficientMap_id` fall back on `change`/`rfl` to see through it.
findings.proposed_change: After the instance, add `@[simp] lemma id_hom (A : LevelCompactRep R G) : (𝟙 A : A ⟶ A).hom = 𝟙 A.rep := rfl` and `@[simp] lemma comp_hom {A B C} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ C) : (f ≫ g).hom = f.hom ≫ g.hom := rfl`. Both are `rfl` by the instance definition. Both rewrite toward the underlying `Rep` morphism, and nothing rewrites back, so there is no loop.
findings.benefit: `simp` can reduce `(f ≫ g).hom` and `(𝟙 A).hom` to the `Rep` category. The existing simp lemmas `mapInvariants_coe` and `forget_map`, and the `Rep` simp set, then apply to composites and identities without manual `change`.

evidence.excerpt: (mapInvariants f U x : B.rep) = f.hom x
